# Real `udevadm monitor --kernel --subsystem-match=block` output, captured on
# this rig as the ordinary user (no root). Events generated with
# `udisksctl loop-setup` on a raw image in /tmp, then `loop-delete`.
#
# First capture: an image with an MBR partition table, no filesystem on the
# partition. One plug, four kernel lines, 13 ms apart - the burst the widget has
# to coalesce. The partition child arrives under the disk's own path and is a
# block-subsystem device too.
monitor will print the received events for:
KERNEL - the kernel uevent

KERNEL[204133.541265] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204133.554137] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204133.554193] add      /devices/virtual/block/loop0/loop0p1 (block)
KERNEL[204133.554347] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
#
# Second capture: the same loop device set up again. The kernel already knows the
# device, so a replug is a change-only burst - no `add` line anywhere. This is
# why "add/change" cannot be read as "only add counts".
KERNEL[204190.125016] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204190.143125] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204190.143271] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204190.143629] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204190.152203] change   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
#
# The other shapes udevadm prints for the same plug, and the lines that are not
# events at all. A real USB stick's own device lines ride other subsystems -
# the filter in udevArgs() is what keeps them from waking the widget.
KERNEL[204133.540981] add      /devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:14.0/usb1/1-1 (usb)
KERNEL[204133.553812] add      /devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:14.0/usb1/1-1/1-1:1.0 (usb)
KERNEL[204133.554001] add      /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204133.554501] remove   /devices/virtual/block/loop0/loop0p1 (block)
KERNEL[204133.554601] bind     /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
KERNEL[204133.554701] unbind   /devices/virtual/block/loop0 (block)
UDEV  [204133.560012] add      /devices/virtual/block/loop0/loop0p1 (block)
KERNEL[204133.560201] change   /devices/virtual/block/nvme0n1 (block)
